author: MicrowaveOnLow
text:
Site doesn’t function with high traffic😭. I really wanted to like Polymarket, but after having essentially the same serious issue happen to me two UFC weekends in a row, I don’t see why I would continue using this platform for live sports trading.

The first time this happened, I went all-in on a fight. The fight ended, I won, but the market stayed stuck in the resolving/settlement process for roughly six hours. During that entire time, my money was basically locked up. I couldn’t withdraw it and, more importantly, I couldn’t use those winnings to trade any of the fights that were happening afterward. By the time the market finally settled and my funds became usable again, the event I actually wanted to trade was basically over.

I originally gave Polymarket the benefit of the doubt and figured it was a one-time technical problem.

Then the exact same type of problem happened again the very next UFC weekend.

This time I placed a two-leg combo/parlay. Both legs won. The app literally shows “2 of 2 won” and shows the value of the winning position in my portfolio, yet hours later my cash balance is still $0 and essentially none of the money is available to trade. At the time of writing this review, it has been around eight hours since the fights ended and I still cannot actually use the money I won.

That completely defeats the purpose of using Polymarket for live sports.

If I’m trading UFC on a Saturday night, I want to be able to win one fight and then use those funds on the next fight. I shouldn’t have to wonder whether winning a bet means my money is going to be locked up for six, eight, or potentially more hours while the platform tries to settle something that has already clearly finished.

And this isn’t an issue I’ve experienced once. It has now happened to me on two consecutive weekends when I was actively trying to trade UFC events.

That is the part I find unacceptable. These are exactly the high-traffic nights when a sports trading platform needs to work correctly. It doesn’t mean much for everything to work perfectly when there is hardly any traffic. The real test is when there is a major sporting event happening and thousands of people are trying to trade at the same time. Based on my experience so far, that is when Polymarket becomes unreliable.

I understand that prediction markets sometimes need time for official resolution and that there can be technical issues. I’m not expecting every market to settle instantaneously. But there is a huge difference between waiting a reasonable amount of time for a result to be confirmed and having clearly winning sports positions remain unusable for six to eight hours.

This is especially frustrating because the app itself can already show that my picks won while simultaneously preventing me from doing anything with the winnings.

Why would I continue keeping money on Polymarket for UFC or other live sports if I have no confidence that I’ll actually be able to use my money after I win?

For someone who only places one bet and then waits until the next day, maybe this isn’t a major issue. But if you are using Polymarket specifically to actively trade a live sporting event throughout the night, this is something you absolutely need to know before depositing money.

Two UFC weekends in a row, I won my positions and then was effectively locked out of using the winnings for hours afterward.

Until Polymarket can reliably handle settlement and make winning funds available during major live events, I personally cannot rely on it as a serious live sports trading platform.

author: johnleslie_pm
text:
This is a textbook oracle manipulation problem, and it's one that prediction market designers have been worried about since the early Augur days. The fundamental issue is that when market resolution depends on a single data source (one weather sensor), the cost of manipulating that oracle can be far less than the payout from the market position. A hairdryer costs $20; the market position could be worth thousands.
The interesting design question is how platforms should handle resolution disputes like this. Polymarket uses UMA's optimistic oracle, which allows anyone to challenge a resolution within a dispute window. But that only works when someone is incentivized to challenge. If the manipulator holds both sides of the market at the right ratio, they can profit even if the resolution is later corrected. Serious prediction markets will eventually need to adopt multi-source oracle designs the way DeFi lending protocols moved to Chainlink-style aggregated price feeds after the flash loan attacks of 2020.
